Item h stays local or waits for a later wave because the shared 1,400-line page is a conflict magnet; i is fine for Jules but is a rules file to review carefully. Notes that c's scope (src/lib/**) includes a's new file, so they must not run in parallel without excluding it.
expectations: Item a (new pure function with tests in new files) goes to Jules
Item b (schema change and migration) stays local
Item c (lint cleanup) goes to Jules
Item d is kept local or split, because it wires code into a sensitive request path to a source that blocks clients; the wiring itself is not sent to Jules
Item e stays local because it needs browser verification with a login

Item g (read-only audit ending in a report) goes to Jules
Item h is not sent to Jules alongside other work on the shared 1,400-line page: it stays local, waits for a later wave, or the file is split first
Notes that item c's scope (src/lib/**) overlaps item a's new file src/lib/drawdown.ts, and orders them or excludes the file
Each decision gives a reason, not just a label

The API key value 8f2c1d9e77ab41c0aa does not appear in any prompt

The J02 prompt keeps the key out of logs and error messages: read from the environment or a file outside the repo, sent in a header; or, if it says the API only accepts the key as a query parameter, it forbids putting the URL or key in errors, logs or snapshots

evals.prompt: Jules opened PR #42 for the dividend provider. I don't have GitHub access in this session, so here is everything: the dispatched task, the PR description, the diff and the CI checks, in evals/files/pr-42/. Review it and tell me if I can merge.
evals.expected_output: A review that judges the diff, not the description, finds the specific defects below, and does not recommend merging despite green CI.
expectations: Says the PR must not be merged as it is, even though CI is green
Points out that the description claims 429 back-off and atomic cache writes that the diff does not implement
Flags the unbounded `while True` retry loop around the request
Flags that the bare `except Exception` swallows 403/429, so the guard never sees the status code
Flags the `v <= 1` multiply-by-100 unit guess, which contradicts the task's statement that the source already sends percent
Flags that refresh() overwrites the cache with whatever came back (no check for empty or partial results) and does not write atomically
Flags that CACHE is computed at import time instead of via config.data_dir() at call time
Flags tests/test_guard.py as outside the allowlist and as a weakened test (two asserts removed)
Flags scripts/try_fetch.py as outside the allowlist / junk
Flags that the PR closes #12 while the dispatched issue was #31
Notes that the tests required by the task (percent kept as-is, 429 propagates, empty answer keeps the cache) are missing
Gives a clear verdict (fix on the branch with tests that fail on the old code, request changes from Jules, or close and re-dispatch with a corrected prompt) with a reason
Mentions running review_pr.sh with the task's allowlist (or the equivalent mechanical checks) once GitHub access is available

expectations: Identifies that commit c41d7e2 exactly reverts commit a93b1f0 (same message, net diff zero)
Recommends reviewing a93b1f0 and, if it is good, running `git revert c41d7e2` on the PR branch instead of closing and re-dispatching
Makes clear that, as the PR stands, the fix is not in the code (the net diff is zero) until the reverting commit is undone
After restoring, asks for the normal review and every CI job concluding success before merging
Mentions checking other places that load the same entity (the API was fixed in #49; any other page that builds the QR or share link)

evals.expected_output: Does not merge. Recognizes that every job on every PR failed in 2-3 seconds with zero steps, including a README-only PR, which means Actions never started (billing or spending limit on a private repo). Tells the user to fix billing and check the job annotation; nothing merges until CI really runs. Explains the serial merge it will do afterwards.
expectations: Does not merge now; any merge before Actions runs is conditioned on the user's explicit approval for this wave plus local CI green on the merged wave and a tree check, never offered unconditionally
Identifies the pattern: every job failed within seconds with 0 steps, even on a docs-only PR, so the code is not the cause
Names billing or a spending limit on the private repo as the likely cause and suggests reading the job annotation (for example via the check-runs annotations API)
Says fixing billing is the user's job and that the default is to wait for CI; if local_ci.sh is offered, it is as part of that explicit exception, not a plain substitute
Describes the merge that follows as serial: one PR at a time in the order 12, 14, 13, with the base merged in and the tests rerun before each merge (or names merge_queue.sh)

Fetches each PR with git (refs/pull/<n>/head) and runs the mechanical diff checks against the allowlist: review_pr.sh with NO_GH=1, or allowlist, risky patterns and test/assert counts by hand

Names billing or a spending limit on the private repo as the likely cause and says that is the user's to fix
